newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power sharply higher amid cold snap.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power sharply higher amid cold snap.

text.p: Spot power prices for peak demand hours in the western U.S. moved sharply higher in reaction to cold weather, market sources said Monday.
"The weather is cold and peak loads have exceeded the hydro(electric) capacity," said one trader.
As a result, there is a big price jump for power generated from the next resource, generally natural gas, he explained.
"There is a big vacuum between price levels. Once people stop needing the extra power for those four hours or so in the middle of the day, prices will go back down," the trader predicted.
He and others said forecasts for warmer temperatures later in the week will bring prices back down within a day or two.

Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) sold out of the 250 megawatts offered during peak hours on Tuesday at $46.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) for California-Oregon border (COB) and $45.00 for Northwest deliveries, the agency said.
Firm, peak electricity at COB for Tuesday was quoted $46.00-48.00 per MWh, up from $16.50-17.50 for Monday.
Traders reported on-peak offers at COB as high as $60.00.
Off-peak COB for Tuesday as also higher at $12.00-13.00.
Tuesday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was higher at $45.00-$47.00, while off-peak was at $12.00-13.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Tuesday was quoted at $38.00-48.00, up from $19.00-20.00.
"We started in the 30s, then the 40s, now the best offer is $60.00," said one trader.
Off-peak PV for Tuesday was quoted $10.00-12.00 per MWh.
Tuesday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were quoted $45.00-50.00, up from $21.00-22.00. Off-peak Four Corners for Tuesday was quoted $10.00-12.00.
But the forward market remained weak with February PV quoted $16.40-16.60, while COB was quoted at $14.10-14.50.
